sections.content: How many people are "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers"?

135,315 people

were counted on the census as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Postal workers, mail sorters and messengers collect, receive, sort and deliver mail, documents, correspondence or messages, either between or within establishments.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers", 16.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" included:

  • cooks
  • local government administrative occupations
  • legal secretaries

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" there were more men than women (75.5% compared with 24.5%).

This means "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 75.5% and women made up 24.5% of "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" included:

  • production, factory and assembly supervisors
  • industrial cleaning process occupations
  • IT managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "postal workers, mail sorters and messengers", 10.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.8%) than self-employed (2.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
